Aetna Member Appeals  
[Address on the denial notice or EOB]

Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for cervical fusion (ACDF)  
Member: Harper Alvarez  
Member ID: W950863136  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA, Tennessee  
Reference number: POC-0FFFC72471-45570  
Requested procedure: CPT 22551, anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at C5-C6

Dear Aetna Member Appeals:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The clinical records support medical necessity under Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0743, Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion. The policy states:

“Cervical laminectomy (and/or an anterior and/or posterior cervical discectomy and fusion) for individuals with herniated discs or other causes of spinal cord or nerve root compression (osteophytic spurring, ligamentous hypertrophy) when all of the following criteria are met:”

The submitted records address the applicable criteria as follows:

1. Cervical disc herniation and nerve-root compression  
The July 13, 2026 MRI documents a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve-root compression. The requested ACDF is directed at the imaged C5-C6 level.

2. Signs and symptoms of neural compression  
The patient has radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness. The examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the C5-C6/C6 imaging findings. These clinical findings are consistent with the documented nerve-root compression.

Aetna’s policy requires that the member have signs or symptoms of neural compression associated with the levels being treated. The records meet that requirement because the symptoms and neurologic findings correspond to the C5-C6 MRI abnormality and right C6 nerve-root compression.

3. Advanced imaging showing significant stenosis or nerve-root compression  
The MRI shows severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve-root compression at C5-C6. This directly addresses the policy requirement that advanced imaging demonstrate qualifying stenosis or nerve-root or spinal-cord compression at the level corresponding with the clinical findings.

4. Failure of conservative treatment  
The patient has completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 27, 2026, through June 22, 2026, with 20 visits documented in the physical-therapy discharge note. The patient also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on April 1, 2026, which provided only two weeks of partial relief.

These records demonstrate substantially more than the policy’s six-week conservative-treatment requirement. The patient’s symptoms have persisted and progressed for 18 months despite supervised therapy, medication, and injection treatment.

5. Functional impact  
The persistent radicular pain, numbness, and weakness interfere with the patient’s function and support the policy requirement concerning limitation of activities of daily living by symptoms of neural compression.

The record also documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status. The requested procedure is being performed by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, for the MRI-confirmed C5-C6 disc herniation and right C6 nerve-root compression.

Because the denial identifies incomplete documentation rather than a determination that the procedure fails the medical-necessity criteria, please conduct a complete reconsideration using the enclosed clinical records. If Aetna believes any specific information remains missing, please identify each missing document or clinical fact precisely and allow the treating surgeon to submit it under this appeal.

Please reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551 at C5-C6. If the request cannot be approved, please provide the specific criterion not met, the clinical information relied upon, the version of CPB 0743 applied, and any supplemental clinical-review criteria used.

Given the progressive symptoms and documented weakness, please also consider this request for expedited appeal review if Aetna’s applicable standards permit expedited handling.

Enclosures:

- Denial notice
- July 13, 2026 cervical MRI report
- Physical-therapy records and discharge note documenting 20 visits from April 27, 2026, through June 22, 2026
- Medication-treatment history
- April 1, 2026 corticosteroid-injection record
- Surgeon’s clinical examination and treatment plan
- Relevant neurologic and orthopedic examination findings
- Any additional records required for review

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected decision date.

Sincerely,

Harper Alvarez
